as_written_in_papers.quote: In the genetic test, the following likely pathogenic variants were detected, in compound heterozygosity, in the LCAT gene: c.580_598del p.(Ala194Serfs*64) and c.619G>A p.(Gly207Ser).

cases.statement: One carrier: a 50-year-old man with end-stage kidney disease, recurrent hemolytic anemia and bilateral corneal opacities, compound heterozygous with c.619G>A p.(Gly207Ser).

people.label: patient
people.zygosity_or_genotype: compound heterozygous (as stated; phase method not reported)
people.key_phenotypes: diffuse bilateral corneal opacities; end-stage kidney disease on hemodialysis after two failed transplants (membranous glomerulonephritis at 21); recurrent hemolytic anemia; low HDL cholesterol; reduced apolipoprotein A

quotes.quote: A 50-year-old white male with end-stage chronic kidney disease, maintained on hemodialysis after two failed renal transplants (1998 and 2013), was referred to the Ophthalmology Department for evaluation of bilateral corneal opacities.
His past medical history included membranous glomerulonephritis diagnosed at the age of 21, complicated by secondary hyperparathyroidism.
He also had a long-standing history of recurrent hemolytic anemia of uncertain etiology.
Slit-lamp examination revealed diffuse corneal opacities involving all layers of the cornea OU (Fig. 1).
The lipid profile showed total cholesterol of 139 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol of 34 mg/dL, LDL cholesterol of 88 mg/dL, and triglycerides of 83 mg/dL.

phenotype_specificity.statement: The authors describe the classical systemic phenotype (corneal opacity, anemia, renal disease) and exclude Tangier disease clinically. No LCAT activity measurement, kidney biopsy re-review or testing of other genes is reported.

quotes.quote: Tangier disease, however, is usually associated with hepatosplenomegaly, neuropathy, and pathognomonic orange tonsils, which were not present in this case.

Our report describes a novel frameshift mutation in the LCAT gene in a patient with the classical systemic phenotype, thereby contributing to the understanding of the genetic basis of this rare disorder.

segregation.statement: No relatives were genotyped. Parents are deceased with no reported renal or eye disease; two brothers and a daughter are described as healthy (untested).

quotes.quote: He has two healthy brothers with no renal or ocular disease and one healthy 20-year-old daughter.

in_trans.statement: The other allele is c.619G>A p.(Gly207Ser). The authors state compound heterozygosity, but no parental or other phase testing is reported (both parents are deceased).

quotes.quote: In the genetic test, the following likely pathogenic variants were detected, in compound heterozygosity, in the LCAT gene: c.580_598del p.(Ala194Serfs*64) and c.619G>A p.(Gly207Ser).

Family history was notable for a father who died at age 72 due to cerebrovascular disease, with no history of renal or ophthalmologic disease, and a mother who died at age 82 due to respiratory disease.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Frameshift (19-bp deletion, predicted p.(Ala194SerfsTer64)) in exon 5 of 6; the authors predict a truncated protein and/or loss of expression through mRNA degradation.

quotes.quote: It is a frameshift variant that occurs in exon 5 (of 6), which introduces a premature stop codon and is predicted to lead to the creation of a truncated protein and/or its loss of expression due to mRNA degradation.

Mutations impairing enzyme activity result in reduced cholesterol esterification, markedly low HDL cholesterol levels, accumulation of unesterified cholesterol, and lipid deposition in multiple tissues, including the cornea, erythrocytes, and kidneys.

population_data_in_papers.statement: The authors state the variant is absent from the gnomAD population database (no version given).

quotes.quote: The c.580_598del p.(Ala194Serfs*64) variant in the LCAT gene has not been described in the literature, nor in the gnomAD population database.

authors_classification.statement: Likely pathogenic, per the authors (criteria not listed).

quotes.quote: Genetic analysis identified compound heterozygosity in the LCAT gene: a novel frameshift variant c.580_598del p.(Ala194Serfs*64), classified as likely pathogenic, and the previously described missense variant c.619G>A p.(Gly207Ser), also classified as likely pathogenic.

concerns: Phase is not shown: no parental testing (parents deceased) and no other phase method reported.
No LCAT enzyme activity or cholesterol esterification measurement is reported; HDL cholesterol is 34 mg/dL.
No transcript is stated in the paper.
The patient's renal history (membranous glomerulonephritis, two failed transplants, immunosuppressants) may confound the renal phenotype.

The other allele c.619G>A p.(Gly207Ser) also appears in batch paper PMID 37138899 (a different person, LCAT-ID0146, with candidate G-lcat-011). The reference this paper cites for c.619G>A (ref. 3) has a title naming other LCAT changes (Arg147Trp and Tyr171Stop).
notes_for_panel: A frameshift in exon 5 of 6 in a patient with corneal opacity, hemolytic anemia and end-stage renal disease; reported as compound heterozygous with c.619G>A, but phase and LCAT activity were not reported.
